steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Brown the ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Drain excess fat and transfer beef to a large pot over medium low heat.. Stir in the onion, green bell pepper, tomatoes, water, rice, chile sauce, salt, brown sugar, cumin, Worcestershire sauce and ground black pepper.
Let this simmer for about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, then transport this to a 2-quart casserole dish. Press down firmly and sprinkle with the shredded Cheddar cheese.
Bake at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) for 10 to 15 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly. Garnish with chopped fresh cilantro.

raw_recipe.headline: Spanish Rice Bake
raw_recipe.description: Ground beef, fresh onion, green bell pepper, tomatoes and rice are simmered in a sweet-hot sauce then baked with Cheddar and garnished with fresh cilantro.

video.description:
Rice refuses to be a side dish in this totally loaded casserole filled with great 
Spanish flavors! Brown ground beef then mix in onion, green bell pepper, 
tomatoes, rice, chili sauce, brown sugar, cumin and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer until rice is cooked and bake topped with a good portion of Cheddar 
cheese for delicious temptation and serve with fresh, fragrant cilantro. 
Everyone will love all the great comfort this delicious dish delivers.

review.reviewBody: I was impressed and thought this was very good!!! My husband however, thought it was too sweet. So next time, I'll omit the brown sugar and reduce the amount of chili sauce by half, replacing the rest with tomato sauce. A little tip for those that those that had a problem with the rice taking longer to cook or that it wasn't finished, it could be from stirring it around too often while the rice is cooking. I did not lift the lid from the pan while it simmered to prevent the steam from escaping (which is what cooks the rice) and it came out perfectly. Also, there's no sense in browing the meat and transferring it to another pot. Just start off browning the meat in a large pot and adding all of the other ingredients as directed.

I made this rice last night and being from Costa Rica, (where we eat rice with just about every meal) the reason why people are experiencing some difficulties with cooking the rice is because the recipe calls for medium low heat, and the only way you can get the rice to cook all the way is by cooking it in just LOW heat. Cooked mine in low heat for about 40 mins added 1.5 cups of medium salsa instead of the water, and a can of corn and once I placed all the ingredients in the casserole dish before baking it I put a layer of refried beans and sprinkle the cheese. I also added some taco seasoning, cumin, and some fresh garlic when I cooked the meat, since i find that the meat picks up all the flavors when you brown it (I will never brown any meat without spices, is like showering without soap!)

I adapted this for my Instant Pot by upping the rice to a heaping cup, which I rinsed first. I also used more peppers (3 mini colored peppers and one jalapeno.) I also added two cloves of crushed garlic. Saute the meat in your pot, then add the vegetables and saute. Then add the spices. I cut the sugar by half and added 1/2 tsp black pepper. Then top with the rinsed rice and the other wet ingredients. Cook on the rice setting and let pressure release manually, stirring to combine afterwards. I let the pot sit on warm for 30 min and it came out perfect. I topped with shredded Mexican cheese blend and chopped cilantro. No need to put in the oven. Great quick meal! The flavor was excellent! Will definitely make it again.

We all liked it. Used it to supplement as a soft taco filling. My changes were to cook everything in the same pan. I cooked the onion with the beef which was so lean, I didn't need to drain any grease. I added all remaining ingredients to the pan with just a bit more water and put a lid on the pan cooking almost 40 mins without removing the lid or stirring ( to make sure rice cooked). The only ingredient changes I made were some red and yellow pepper for the green as it was what I had and I used petite diced canned tomatoes. I did by mistake add 3/4 c. chile sauce as I read the recipe wrong. It didn't hurt it, and in fact I might just add the whole bottle next time because there wasn't much left in it. Once it had cooked on the stove top, I removed the lid, stirred it and sprinkled cheese on top then placed the pan in the oven for 10 mins. My husband commented later he really liked it. And he had tried to talk me out of making it!

i made this and it was delicious. Changes I made was i used reg white rice , added green onion with the sweet onion and i made this in a cast iron skillet and then put the skillet into the oven for convenience and flavor. Definitely will do this one again.

Yummy! Made (instant) rice on its own and then added when simmering (no need to then add any water). Used sriracha/ketchup mix (1/4 cup sriracha plenty- maybe even use a bit less next time)cause I didn’t have any chilli sauce. And didn’t bother with the oven, just let cheese melt while on stove.

I made exactly as written, but with the addition of 1 cup of water as others had suggested. It’s very tasty, and we all liked it. You know what it reminds me of? A deconstructed stuffed pepper! Next time I make it I’m going to try it with more chopped bell pepper. This could also be made on the stove with a covered skillet if you didn’t have an oven or didn’t want to bake it.

It was really good. I made a couple substitutions based on what was in my cabinet. I used fire roasted tomatoes with garlic and green chile enchilada sauce.

I also used my Instant Pot to brown the meat along with the onions , then pressure cooked everything for 15 minutes. 

it came out really well.

Fantastic taste and not difficult to make! I did change it a little the second time I made it and used a spicy, chunky tomato sauce instead of the canned tomatoes. It tasted even better to us but we also love spicy foods. I recommend you cook the dish for longer than 30 minutes on the stove as the rice is borderline hard each time I've made it- nothing 5 more minutes wouldn't fix. This is definitely a keeper!

It was easy to make and I did use just one pan- my cast iron paella pan worked great. However, I thought it was a little bland and needed to add some hot sauce ( your flavor choice) when serving. I covered it tightly, cooked it on low, only stirred once as suggested and my rice was perfect. Finished off in broiler to get some nice color on the cheese

Made this with some leftover ground beef and cooked rice. Followed most of the directions but didn't need all the water to cook the rice. Let it simmer together. Next time I will add the meat to the rice to pull in the flavors. I also removed tomatoes since kids don't like it and added jalapenos for some spice. Great dish for the family that is easy!
This was excellent. Husband had left overs which he never has. Easy to make and delicious. Been making since 2019.

We really enjoyed this! I used ground elk, which is extra lean, so added avocado oil and extra onions for moisture. Added additional seasonings-garlic, onion & green chili powders and minced fresh garlic. Also added diced green chilies and corn. It was delicious, fast, easy and obviously versatile! Now we’ll see how the leftovers freeze??

No changes except made 1/2 the recipe for the two of us! I'd say we ate 3/4 of it! Amazing, we both agreed and will definitely make again. After original part, I put it in a casserole dish rather than skillet to finish, and it was great! I loved that I had EVERYTHING on hand, as I've shopping my freezer and pantry! Thanks for this one!
Saw it today, conquered it tonight. Read tons of 5 Star reviews and tweaked recipe based on what I already had, but shopped for what was necessary. Delicious. A keeper for sure.

This is one of our favorite recipes. It reheats really well, is easy to make. I know we're not supposed to make substitutions but I skip the pepper and onion and just add the same amount of premade salsa to save myself the chopping and it comes out like a dream. Sometimes I add a can of corn to it and it's like a complete meal!

This was good. We used it for taco filling. I used beef broth instead of water. I had to use twice as much liquid and cook longer so the rice would cook. But after reading others, that is probably because I kept taking the lid off and stirring it. Also, next time, I will cook all in 1 pan on the stove as others suggested.
Excellent
This was delicious. I usually don’t like Spanish rice, just make it for my husband, but this was great. Will put this on my dinner list.

This recipe is worth keeping great taste no hassle to make. My husband and I enjoyed will definitely make it again. I did use a mixture of red and green bell peppers, also used beef broth instead of water and used 1.5 cups didn't have plain canned tomatoes so used Italian style was perfect.
